paper.title_en: Production Memory of the $^{225}\mathrm{Ra}$-$^{225}\mathrm{Ac}$ Clock in Neutron-Star Merger Ejecta
paper.abstract_en: Radioactive nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta carry information about both their abundance and their production history. Using the $^{225}\mathrm{Ra}$-$^{225}\mathrm{Ac}$ sequence, we establish exact conditions linking a surviving isotope partition to the time available for parent decay. An Ac fraction of 0.1 produced solely through Ra decay requires at least 2.456 days, providing a direct consistency test for proposed source states. We show that subsequent activity retains additional production memory: two histories with the same mean birth time can produce different response crossings. This distinction is captured analytically and separates mean chronology from the influence of the production-time distribution. A controlled radiation calculation then shows how deposition and photon escape transform the nuclear contrast into a common light-curve pivot for fixed ejecta properties. The results connect nuclear production chronology to late-time merger emission and provide benchmarks for nucleosynthesis and radiation-transport calculations.
